context.body: Deuteronomy interprets the crisis through refusal, distorted divine motive, remembered care, and unbelief.
context.label: Narrative or literary frame

observations.body: Moses says the people would not go up, rebelled, and accused the LORD of hating them and bringing them out for destruction.
observations.label: The retelling centers refusal, accusation, and fear: action

observations.body: He recalls answering that the LORD would fight as in Egypt and carry them as a man carries his son, yet they did not believe.
observations.label: The retelling centers refusal, accusation, and fear: response

observations.body: would not go up · rebelled · LORD hated us · carried you · did not believe
observations.label: Words in Deuteronomy 1:26–33

payload.posture: Read Deuteronomy 1:26–33 as presumption and later retelling evidence before carrying it into another source.
payload.tension: The retelling gives Moses the answering speech that Numbers distributes between Caleb, Joshua, Moses, and divine speech.
payload.title: The retelling centers refusal, accusation, and fear
